title: Retaining an array at each recursive level creates quadratic space
summary: When every recursive level also holds a local array, peak space sums the array lengths across all simultaneously unreturned levels.
context: Here n is a positive integer. Whenever k > 0, each call quadratic_recur(k) allocates an array nums of length k before calling quadratic_recur(k - 1). The figure omits the final call quadratic_recur(0), which allocates no array, simplifying the base case and return onto the row for argument 1; the actual code returns immediately at argument 0.
description: From left to right, the figure arranges three columns—"Length of array nums", "Recurse downward", and "Return upward"—connecting each array length horizontally to its call. A brace labeled "Recursion depth n" spans the n levels that allocate arrays, with ellipses for intermediate calls. At the row for argument 1, an arrow labeled "Reach the base case" crosses to the right column, where return 0 entries are linked upward.

frames.title: Retaining an array at each recursive level creates quadratic space
frames.explanation: While each upper call waits for its lower call to return, its local array remains live in memory. At the bottom, summing their lengths gives 1 + 2 + … + (n - 1) + n = n(n + 1)/2, pointing to Quadratic O(n²). Although the actual code adds one extra stack frame at argument 0 without allocating an array, the O(n) call-stack overhead does not change the O(n²) peak space dominated by those arrays.
